articles.title: The best Oura Ring alternatives, tested by our editors
articles.summary: We tested smart rings from Ultrahuman and Samsung to find our favorite alternatives to the Oura Ring.
articles.body: Oura, maker of the popular Oura Ring, recently announced that it is investing in U.S. manufacturing operations in Fort Worth, Texas, partly in order to bolster the specialized and evolving needs of its military partnerships. The brand has worked across the U.S. Department of Defense, its largest enterprise customer, since 2019. The Oura announcement has been met with immediate backlash online. However, Oura has released statements to press and on its subreddit, explaining that no Oura Ring user’s data is shared with the DoD except when you are “enrolled in a Department of Defense (DoD) health or human-performance program that uses Oura Ring, and you have consented to share your data with that program.” The Oura Ring is one of the most popular smart rings on the market — it’s an excellent wearable with a sleek design and an intuitive app. But if you're looking for an alternative smart ring based on the recent news, we have you covered. I’ve tested wearables and smart rings for years, and rounded up some of the best (subscription-free) Oura Ring alternatives below. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best Oura Ring alternatives of 2026 Our top picks come from tech brands like Ultrahuman and Samsung. Below each recommendation, I share specifications to consider when shopping. Best overall This fully-featured smart ring tracks your health, wellness and fitness metrics, with a big emphasis on actionable insights, and it’s become an NBC Selected favorite for Oura Ring alternatives. While it has a higher price up front than the Oura Ring 5, you won’t find any mandatory subscription fees here, which can add up over time. You’ll also get exceptional battery life, up to 45 days worth. The ring was also designed with data protection in mind — it’s processed in a secure system with up to a year of on-PRO Charger storage, according to Ultrahuman. I previously tested the Ring Air and loved its features, many of which carry over to the Ring Pro. It can send you notifications for things like your optimal caffeine window for the day, ideal sun exposure and details around your circadian phases.” Learn more in my Ultrahuman Ring Air review. Best for Samsung If you already own a Samsung smartphone, the Samsung Galaxy Ring is the best smart ring to get. It tracks very similar metrics and analysis to the Oura and Ultrahuman rings, but it has a standout design that sets it apart from the competition. It’s the most comfortable smart ring I’ve tested — it’s very light, and the concave design looks sleek on my finger. It comes with a transparent, wired charging case that I love, especially compared to Oura and Ultrahuman’s charging docks. Plus it syncs seamlessly with other Samsung smartphones and smartwatches. Please note that it is only compatible with Android smartphones — iPhone owners should look at our other options. Best budget The Ringconn Gen 2 Air costs $199 and does not have a subscription fee — it costs much less than the Oura Ring and every other smart ring on this list. Despite its lowest price, it has an up to 10-day battery life, much longer than its competitors. It tracks similar metrics and scores with sleep, health and fitness, including Health Alerts to indicate potential signs of illness. If you want features like sleep apnea detection, a wireless charging case and 14 days of battery life (up from 10), consider the pricier RingConn Gen 3 instead. How I picked the best Oura Ring alternatives To pick the best alternatives to the Oura Ring, I tried smart rings from brands like Ultrahuman and Samsung, keeping the following criteria in mind when using them: Price: One of the main reasons people search for Oura Ring alternatives is price: it’s one of the most expensive smart rings, plus it has a monthly subscription fee. As such, I focused on alternatives that cost less than the Oura Ring.Ease of use: A smart ring should be easy to use while giving interesting, informative and actionable data. I tested each smart ring app, looking at glanceable data as well as customization options.Compatibility: I noted when products were compatible with iPhone, Android or both, and generally preferred products with dual-compatibility How to shop for Oura Ring alternatives There are a few things to keep in mind when shopping for any smart ring, regardless of brand. Try a sizing kit first Smart ring sizing is not universal — each ring fits a little differently, even if you order the same size. Purchase the brand’s sizing kit first to find your perfect fit before ordering the actual smart ring. Prioritize comfort There’s a saying in photography that the best camera is the one you have with you. The same is true for health and fitness tracking: the best smart ring for you is the one that you’ll actually wear daily. Consider which finger you’ll wear your smart ring, and if it will rub uncomfortably against other jewelry you may wear. If you’re not a ring person, it’s unlikely a smart ring is going to change your mind and be more comfortable than a wrist-based fitness tracker. Double-check compatibility Like smartwatches, smart rings are compatible with Android and/or iPhone devices. Make sure you purchase one that is compatible with your phone — iPhone owners shouldn’t purchase the Android-only Samsung Galaxy Ring, for example. Why trust NBC Selected? Harry Rabinowitz is a former reporter at NBC Selected who covered technology and fitness including recent stories on smartwatches, running shoes, cameras and more. He test smart rings and wearable tech regularly, and leveraged his experience using smart rings as well as that of NBC Selected staffers. articles.title: Bengaluru researcher wins Google PhD fellowship
articles.summary: Bengaluru NCBS PhD researcher Surya Sarathi Das wins 2026 Google PhD Fellowship to develop AI tools for predicting cervical cancer recurrence risk.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A doctoral researcher at National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) has been selected for the 2026 Google PhD fellowship, becoming the first PhD student from the institute to receive the recognition.Surya Sarathi Das, who works in the laboratory of professor Sabarinathan Radhakrishnan at NCBS, has been selected in the health research category, representing India. The fellowship, supported by Google.org, will fund his research exploring how AI can help assess the risk of cervical cancer recurrence using routinely available digital pathology data.Das’ team has identified a molecular marker that could help distinguish patients at higher risk of relapse. With the fellowship support, Das plans to develop and evaluate AI models that can predict this biomarker directly from digital pathological data. This could potentially make risk assessment more affordable and accessible.“Through my PhD research, I have been trying to understand why some patients with cervical cancer experience recurrence while others do not. With support from Google, I hope to take this work further by exploring AI-based approaches to predict this marker and assess recurrence risks,” Das said.Das is among 148 researchers selected for the 2026 fellowship across 38 countries. articles.title: Wild romance: Gujarat plans ‘welcome suites’ for tiger brides
articles.summary: Gujarat plans 5-hectare acclimatisation enclosures in Dang and Narmada to introduce tigresses to Ratanmahal’s lone tiger before release, pending NTCA approval.
articles.body: AHMEDABAD: Gujarat’s lone tiger may soon have a pair of potential mates, but before the tigresses can venture into his territory in Ratanmahal, the forest department is preparing adaptation enclosures for them. The two enclosures, likely to span five hectares each, will serve as temporary homes where the striped queens can settle into their new surroundings while the resident male gets a chance to pick up their scent and hear their calls before any encounter in the wild.The department has floated tenders for two enclosures — one in Dang and the other in Narmada district — which are expected to be ready within 45 days. While options ranging from two to five hectares are under consideration, officials favour the larger model. Two to three proposals have been submitted to the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), which will decide the approach to be adopted.The idea is to give each tigress time to acclimatise to her new surroundings before she is released into the wild. The enclosures could also help the resident male become familiar with the presence of a potential mate through scent and vocalisations. Officials believe such an introduction could help them understand how the male responds to the arrival of females in the landscape, without immediately bringing the animals face to face.Forest officials cited an interesting example from Sakkarbaug Zoo, where a male lion would often approach an enclosure after hearing a lioness’s call. They hope to study whether the presence or calls of a tigress could evoke a similar response from the male tiger.Principal chief conservator of forests Jaipal Singh confirmed the department was considering five-hectare enclosures for the tigresses. “The facilities could subsequently be used for herbivore breeding once the tigresses are released,” Singh said. A senior forest officer in Gandhinagar said strengthening the ungulate population would help build a sustainable prey base, a critical requirement if the landscape is to support a breeding tiger population in the long run.The exercise is also about preparing Gujarat’s forest personnel for an animal whose behaviour is markedly different from that of the Asiatic lion. Unlike lions, which live in prides, tigers are largely solitary and fiercely territorial. Officials, whose field experience has centred on lions, want to understand the tigresses’ movement patterns, aggression levels and responses to unfamiliar surroundings before releasing them. articles.title: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky praised Chinese AI models, calling them 'Fast and Cheap'; now US government may ask the company to share his 'China preference' with all Americans
articles.summary: In October 2025, Brian Chesky, co-founder and CEO of the San Francisco-based online accommodation booking giant, said Airbnb \"relies heavily\" on Alibaba's
articles.body: In October 2025, Brian Chesky, co-founder and CEO of the San Francisco-based online accommodation booking giant, said Airbnb "relies heavily" on Alibaba's Qwen models to power its AI-driven customer service agent. Chesky said that ChatGPT's integration abilities were not "quite ready" for Airbnb's needs. In contrast, Alibaba's Qwen model was "very good" and "also fast and cheap", he said in an interview with Bloomberg. Now, it seems he will have to go public with his 'Chinese preferences' for AI models. According to a report in Reuters, "Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, a bid to discourage reliance on the technology without imposing new restrictions that could anger industry or Beijing." As per the report, the Treasury Department and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) have discussed ‌the plan, which would apply to companies such as Airbnb. The company uses Qwen, an AI model made by China's Alibaba to power its AI customer service agent. Under the plan, companies like Airbnb would be required to post that information on their websites.US government proposal aims to 'name and shame' companies using Chinese AIThe proposal is said to show that officials are looking at ways to discourage companies use of ⁠Chinese AI models through a "name and shame" campaign while sticking to a broader anti-regulation stance on AI.The consideration comes as Chinese-made open-weight models are gaining ground with US companies because they are cheaper ​than proprietary AI tools from top US labs OpenAI and Anthropic, and perform well enough. This has worried China hawks, who fear that Beijing is using such models — like Moonshot AI's Kimi, DeepSeek or Qwen — to hook US companies so they will become dependent ‌on Chinese ⁠AI.In July, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the Trump administration could sanction Chinese AI companies if they were found to be guilty of intellectual property theft via distillation of American models. Distillation is the process of training smaller AI models using the output of larger ones as part of an effort to lower the costs of training a powerful new AI tool.The issue reportedly attracted the ⁠attention of Congress. Republican US Representatives Andrew Garbarino of New York and John Moolenaar of Michigan, who chair the House Homeland Security Committee and the House select committee on China, respectively, launched an investigation into American companies' use of Chinese AI this year.Airbnb CEO defends company using Chinese modelsIn an interview to Bloomberg TV in May this year, Chesky clarified that Airbnb is not a customer of Alibaba or other Chinese companies. “We are not providing data to any Chinese companies. They don’t have access to any data,” he said. Airbnb CEO further added, “We’re primarily using a variety of open-source models, including U.S. open-source models. An open-source model does not have access to data. It doesn’t work that way. I think people need to understand how this stuff works.”Earlier this year, the US House committees on China and homeland security sent a letter to Airbnb, asking for clarifications on its use of Chinese AI models as part of an investigation into what they described as a Chinese campaign to “accelerate its AI capabilities by exploiting American innovation.”They pointed to comments by Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky, who said last year that the company is "relying a lot" on the Qwen model, describing it as "very good" and "fast and cheap."Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: ‘Any pretty woman from China is considered spy’: Trump discussed Huang affair with Xi
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump said former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang came up only “briefly” during his conversation with Chinese President Xi
articles.body: US President Donald Trump said former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang came up only “briefly” during his conversation with Chinese President Xi Jinping, before describing Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang as a “pretty woman” and insisting she was “a businesswoman who bought chips”, not a spy. Trump insisted that the leaders' discussions largely centred on artificial intelligence (AI).The US president also described Huang's reported departure from the chipmaker as a “tragedy”, calling him a “brilliant man”.In an interview with Fox News, broadcast during the network's The Ingraham Angle on Wednesday, Trump was asked about whether Huang's situation had featured in his conversation with Xi.Also Read|'You don't kick Michael Jordan off a winning team': Musk backs Jensen Huang, questions Nvidia move“We did not discuss it. I might have referred to it just briefly because it's such a tragedy. It's a tragedy. He's such a brilliant man,” Trump said, adding, "We need to take care of our geniuses. There are not many of them."Describing his discussions with the Chinese President, Trump indicated that AI had been a key subject during their dinner conversation.“We spoke the whole evening, and we talked about that (AI),” he said.Trump also praised Huang's contribution to the technology industry, saying, “Some people can’t be replaced. He was ten years ahead.”The remarks come amid controversy surrounding Huang's reported departure from Nvidia following allegations about his personal relationships, including an alleged affair with the Chinese businesswoman. The claims have also drawn attention to potential national security implications.According to people familiar with the matter, US intelligence officials are examining Alice Huang's alleged connections to China's security ministry and whether she may have passed on sensitive information.Trump, however, said he was unaware of any established national security threat linked to the claims. “I haven't heard that,” Trump said when asked whether the reported affair posed a national security risk.“I haven't heard that she was a spy,” he added. Trump also addressed questions about Alice Huang's background and the scrutiny surrounding her reported links to China.“It was a woman. It was a pretty woman. And any pretty woman that comes from China, they consider her to be a spy. I haven't heard that she was a spy. She was a businesswoman who bought chips,” he said.“Who knows if they were bought right or wrong. But I can tell you we allow them to buy. We want to make money,” Trump added.Huang had previously voiced support for Trump's AI agenda and met the US president several times as Nvidia sought to secure access to the Chinese market for its chips. The company's business interests have been closely linked to Washington's export-control policies amid growing technological competition between the US and China.Trump's comments come as the leaders of China, the United States and Russia are set to hold their first-ever trilateral meeting on Thursday in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Jinping, Trump and Russian president Vladimir Putin will meet for talks that Beijing says will focus on “safeguarding world peace” and promoting strategic stability.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Human' is Cambridge dictionary's word of '26
articles.summary: London: Fears of artificial intelligence inspired the Cambridge dictionary to flip back to the 15th century for the word that best captures the 2026
articles.body: London: Fears of artificial intelligence inspired the Cambridge dictionary to flip back to the 15th century for the word that best captures the 2026 cultural zeitgeist."Human," the dictionary's word of the year, is not just a throwback but also a backlash of sorts that reflects the debate over how AI has blurred the lines between machines and people. "AI is changing how we talk about being human," said Colin McIntosh, the dictionary's lexicographer. "Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children."The adjective derived from the Latin "humanus" and in use since the 1450s is defined by Cambridge as "having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines." Dictionaries typically choose a novel word or an existing word that has taken on a new meaning.AI has factored heavily in Word of the Year distinctions across several dictionaries in recent years. "AI" itself was chosen by Collins Dictionary in 2023 - a year when Cambridge picked "hallucinate," in reference to the tendency of AI to fabricate information. Merriam-Webster last year named "slop" its word of the year for low quality content produced by AI while Collins went with "vibe coding" for the AI-assisted software development method.Other word contenders for 2026 included "agent," for an AI system that can make decisions and operate without human control and "analogue" for experiences or objects not involving the internet or digital technology. apYou use AI every day. articles.title: Bhakra canal bridge collapses on Patiala-Sangrur bypass; 2 trucks trapped, drivers hurt
articles.summary: PATIALA: A portion of an iron truss bridge over the Bhakra canal near Pasiana village on the Patiala-Sangrur bypass (NH-7) collapsed early Thursday
articles.body: PATIALA: A portion of an iron truss bridge over the Bhakra canal near Pasiana village on the Patiala-Sangrur bypass (NH-7) collapsed early Thursday morning, trapping two loaded trailers in the damaged section. No casualties were reported, though both truck drivers sustained injuries and were rescued by local villagers before being shifted to a hospital.The incident occurred around 5.30am on the carriageway leading from Patiala towards Sangrur. According to police, both heavy vehicles were travelling in the same direction — from the new bus stand towards Sangrur-Bathinda — and were crossing the bridge side by side when the structure suddenly gave way.One of the two trapped trucks caught fire shortly after the collapse, triggering panic in the area. Fire brigade teams rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control. Although the trucks got stuck in the collapsed section, they did not plunge into the canal, which flowed well below the damaged span. However, following the collapse, water from the Bhakra canal began overflowing onto parts of the damaged structure.Police completely closed the damaged carriageway and implemented traffic diversions. While the parallel carriageway from Sangrur towards Patiala remains intact, authorities have barred heavy vehicles from using it as a precaution.Station House Officer (SHO) of Pasiana police station, Sub Inspector Pavittar Singh, said, "Because the pillars broke from above, there is a risk on the other side too, so we cannot allow heavy traffic there right now." He added that heavy vehicles were being diverted through the city under the supervision of traffic personnel.Teams from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the district administration reached the spot to assess the damage and initiate a technical probe. Police confirmed that no repair work was underway on the bridge at the time of the collapse.According to preliminary inputs from the Public Works Department (B&R), the collapsed span was an older iron truss bridge originally constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) in 2000 on land acquired by the B&R department. The stretch was later widened from two lanes to four lanes, with a parallel bridge built by the PWD, which remains intact."The entire road stretch, along with its records, was handed over to the NHAI in 2021, and they have been maintaining it since," said Navdeep Singh Singla, Executive Engineer (XEN), B&R Sangrur, who looked after this section. He added that the exact cause of the collapse could only be determined after a formal inspection by NHAI officials.While technical experts examine whether a sudden combined load from two parallel overloaded trucks triggered the collapse, officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, have not ruled out structural weakening caused by missing or stolen bolts from the truss bridge.NHAI site engineer Abhishek Chauhan, when asked about the possible cause of the collapse and the last structural audit, said, "We are conducting the inspection at the spot after which we will be able to share the details and reason behind the collapse."You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.summary: US president Donald Trump on Thursday opposed international efforts to regulate or restrict the development of superintelligence (SI), saying Washington
articles.body: US president Donald Trump on Thursday opposed international efforts to regulate or restrict the development of superintelligence (SI), saying Washington would not allow measures that could stifle the technology.Addressing the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, China, he described SI as the biggest technological transformation since the Industrial Revolution.“The United States is also proud to be the world leader in superintelligence, SI, the greatest technological transformation since the Industrial Revolution. It's amazing when you say that, but it seems to be true. Americans invented—we just invented SI, and it is unleashing extraordinary prosperity and growth for people all around the globe,” Trump said.While promoting the technology’s potential, Trump acknowledged that its development could carry risks and called for safeguards to manage them.“We have to watch it. We have to be careful. We have to cherish it. It's almost completely good, but it's got some bad elements, so we have to be very careful in managing those bad elements,” he said.However, he ruled out global regulatory measures, arguing that they could impede innovation.“So we oppose any form of globalist regulation or anything to control or stifle SI, and we won't allow that to happen, frankly,” Trump added.Trump also used the address to highlight his administration’s economic record, claiming that inflation had remained below two per cent over the preceding three months.“The last 3 months, inflation was down to a number that was not expected. We were able to do a real job. You know, a lot of other countries are having difficulty with that, but we've gotten it less than 2% for the last 3 months,” he said.He claimed the US had secured commitments worth $22.2 trillion in new investments and generated $25 trillion in new wealth up to November 1. Trump also said investment in new equipment had risen by 21 per cent this year and exports had reached a record high.He attributed the claimed gains to tax cuts, deregulation and trade agreements, saying the administration had concluded more than 20 deals. He also indicated that further agreements with major economies were being negotiated.Trump promoted US energy exports, referring to an approved liquefied natural gas pipeline project in Alaska intended to supply Asian markets. He also said American oil companies were “moving in” to Venezuela, adding: “We’re doing tremendous business in Venezuela.”His comments on SI come days after the US and nine partner countries, including India, signed the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity on November 15. articles.title: 'He is my friend': Trump, Putin hold talks ahead of trilateral meeting with Xi on APEC sidelines
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump held bilateral talks with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin, ahead of a trilateral discussion with Chinese President Xi
articles.body: US President Donald Trump held bilateral talks with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin, ahead of a trilateral discussion with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.The meeting was held on the sidelines of APEC summit in Chinese city of Shenzhen.Trump expressed optimism ahead of the meeting"A lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start", he said."We will have a second meeting later on," he added.The meeting comes amid heightened diplomatic activity involving Washington, Moscow and Beijing, with the three leaders expected to discuss nuclear disarmament, the Iran conflict, the Russia-Ukraine war and global trade. The proposed trilateral engagement is being closely watched as a possible opportunity to address some of the most pressing geopolitical challenges.Trump arrived at the APEC venue earlier in the day, where he was welcomed by Xi. The US president subsequently met Putin, with the two leaders exchanging handshakes before joining other world leaders for a group photograph.The bilateral engagement between Trump and Putin comes a day after the Russian president held extensive discussions with Xi, reaffirming the strength of Moscow's strategic partnership with Beijing.Trump-Putin meeting ahead of trilateral talksThe Trump-Putin meeting assumes importance as Washington and Moscow seek to address differences over the Ukraine war and the future of nuclear arms control.Trump had indicated before departing for Asia that the proposed discussions with Putin and Xi would cover several major international issues, including nuclear disarmament, Iran, Ukraine and economic relations."We're going to be talking about denuclearisation...We'll talk about Iran," Trump told reporters ahead of his departure.He also identified the Russia-Ukraine war as a key subject of discussion."We'll also talk about my favourite subject, Ukraine. Ukraine is losing. Ukraine and Russia are losing 25,000 souls per month, so we'll be talking about that. We'll also discuss economics and trade," Trump said.The proposed trilateral meeting would bring together the leaders of three major powers at a time when diplomatic efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict have faced challenges.The prospect of discussions involving Washington and Moscow without Ukraine's direct participation has also raised concerns in Kyiv and among its European partners.Xi and Putin reaffirm strategic partnershipAhead of Trump's arrival, Xi and Putin held bilateral discussions in Shenzhen on Wednesday, reaffirming their commitment to strengthening economic, political and strategic cooperation.Xi described the relationship between China and Russia as resilient amid international uncertainty, saying their ties "stand as firm as a mountain amid wind and rain".He called on both countries to adopt a long-term strategic approach and shoulder greater responsibilities as major powers in shaping the international order."We must firmly shoulder the responsibilities expected of major powers, lead and advance the multipolarisation of the world and the democratisation of international relations," Xi said.Putin, meanwhile, described political cooperation between Moscow and Beijing as constructive despite the challenging international environment."Russian-Chinese political cooperation is working favourably and constructively in a difficult political situation," Putin stated."We are committed to constructive approaches to form a fairer multipolar world order," he added.The two leaders also discussed the need to expand cooperation across sectors, with Xi describing their partnership as a model of equality, mutual respect and mutually beneficial cooperation.According to Russian media reports, the discussions continued over a working breakfast in Shenzhen on Wednesday.Putin criticises economic restrictions, calls for fairer world orderPutin also addressed business representatives at the APEC CEO Summit, where he criticised the use of tariffs, sanctions and export restrictions as instruments of geopolitical and economic pressure.He argued that countries were increasingly seeking greater economic sovereignty and independence amid changes in the global geopolitical landscape."The regional model serves as a vivid example of strengthening a fairer, more democratic and equal world order," Putin said, referring to developments in the Asia-Pacific region.The Russian president criticised attempts by established economic powers to restrict the growth of emerging economies, arguing that such measures undermined fair competition and could ultimately hurt the countries imposing them.Putin acknowledged that tariffs, export restrictions and sanctions continued to affect economic development."But they are not capable of fully stopping growth or destroying the economies of the competition," he added.He also expressed expectations of "great use" from the proposed trilateral meeting involving Trump, Xi and himself.Nuclear arms control and Iran on trilateral agendaThe proposed meeting comes at a sensitive moment for international nuclear arms control following the expiration of the New START treaty between the United States and Russia in February 2026.Trump has expressed interest in negotiating a new nuclear arms control framework that would include China alongside Washington and Moscow.However, Beijing has traditionally resisted joining such negotiations, pointing to the considerably larger nuclear arsenals maintained by the United States and Russia.The Iran conflict is another issue expected to feature in the discussions, alongside disagreements over international trade, tariffs, technology restrictions and global supply chains.China has described the proposed trilateral engagement as being of "ground-breaking significance", with the potential to safeguard global peace and promote strategic stability among major powers.The APEC summit has consequently emerged as an important diplomatic platform for Washington, Moscow and Beijing to engage on issues ranging from nuclear security to regional conflicts and the future of the global economic order.You use AI every day. articles.title: Hindu temple attack plot: Illinois man indicted on multiple 'terrorism' charges
articles.summary: A 19-year-old man arrested last month over an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois has been indicted on multiple
articles.body: A 19-year-old man arrested last month over an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois has been indicted on multiple "terrorism" charges, news agency Reuters cited police on Wednesday.Alexandros Paporakis, a resident of Palatine, a Chicago suburb, was arrested in October after an individual alerted police about receiving concerning electronic communications from him, Palatine police said.A Cook County grand jury indicted Paporakis on six counts of terrorism, two counts of attempted terrorism and two counts of armed violence. All are felonies. The grand jury also added nine counts of making a terrorist threat, police said.The indictment includes additional weapons-related charges, including possession of a firearm without a serial number. Paporakis remains in custody, with his next court appearance scheduled for Thursday, police said.According to US media reports, an attorney representing Paporakis said he planned to plead not guilty to the charges.The alleged plot to attack the temple was reportedly planned for October 11, the first day of Navratri. The incident triggered concern among South Asian and Hindu Americans and drew condemnation from several US lawmakers.The ministry of external affairs had said it was "deeply concerned" by the incident and its "racist nature."Detectives believed Paporakis may have been planning an attack on October 11, potentially targeting a Hindu place of worship in Aurora, around 40 miles (65 km) southwest of Palatine, police said.During a search of Paporakis' residence last month, detectives recovered several items, including a tactical vest containing body armour and a patch displaying imagery associated with white supremacist extremism, police said.Investigators also examined electronic communications and a document attributed to Paporakis titled "Why I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter's Manifesto)".According to police, the document contained statements expressing "white supremacist and extremist ideologies", including references to violence against people of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian descent.Human rights advocates have said anti-South Asian hate in the US has increased in recent years, citing factors such as anti-immigration rhetoric and policies and the rise of white supremacist movements.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meet Abrielle Fonder, the 12-year-old South Dakota girl who sells pumpkins and homemade potpourri to raise money for homeless cats and dogs at a local animal shelter
articles.summary: A small pumpkin patch and a collection of homemade potpourri have become an unusual way for a 12-year-old girl in South Dakota to support animals waiting
articles.body: A small pumpkin patch and a collection of homemade potpourri have become an unusual way for a 12-year-old girl in South Dakota to support animals waiting for homes. Abrielle Fonder began growing pumpkins to sell, with the proceeds going towards the Sioux Falls Humane Society. She later added handmade potpourri to her fundraising efforts, giving her another way to contribute. The money is intended to help the shelter meet the needs of cats and dogs, including food, accommodation and medical treatment. For Abrielle, the project is tied to a simple concern: not every animal has a family to care for it.How Abrielle turned her hobbies into a fundraiserAbrielle's initiative began with planting pumpkins. What started as a growing project gradually developed into a small fundraising activity, with the produce being sold to collect money for the local animal shelter.She did not stop there. Alongside the pumpkins, Abrielle began preparing homemade potpourri, which she also sells to raise funds. The earnings from both activities go to the Sioux Falls Humane Society, where donations help provide everyday care for animals awaiting adoption, as reported by Dakota News Now.The approach has given her two different ways to raise money through things she can make or grow herself. Rather than relying on a single seasonal sale, she has been able to add another product to her efforts.A young fundraiser's commitment to animals without homesAbrielle's interest in the shelter is rooted in the circumstances of animals without permanent homes. She believes that cats and dogs deserve a safe place to live, even if they have not yet found someone willing to adopt them.Speaking about her motivation, she explained that she wanted to help because some animals do not have good homes. Her own pet, Sunkist, is also part of her life, and her interest in animal welfare is something she hopes to continue as she grows older.For now, the pumpkin and potpourri sales give her a practical way to contribute. The money is directed towards needs that shelters face while caring for animals, from feeding them to arranging medical attention and providing a place for them to stay.Humane Society praises Abrielle's efforts to help animalsThe effort has also drawn appreciation from the organisation receiving the money. Jami Gates Grieve, executive director of the Sioux Falls Humane Society, spoke about the amount of work involved in Abrielle's project, particularly given her age.She pointed out that the girl had taken on the process of planting pumpkins, preparing them for sale and raising money before choosing to give the proceeds to the shelter. The contribution helps support the organisation's work with cats and dogs that need care.Abrielle's father, Mark Fonder, also spoke about what he hopes she takes away from the experience. He said he would like her efforts to encourage other children to find ways of giving back to their communities.The Humane Society has also emphasised that contributions do not need to be large to be useful. Donations of different sizes can help cover the costs involved in looking after animals until suitable homes are found.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A US partnership turned 2.5 million pounds of unsold food and drinks into renewable energy and fertiliser in 15 months; here's how the waste recovery process works
articles.summary: A US partnership between refrigerated storage company US Cold Storage and food waste recovery company Divert has turned unsold food and beverage products
articles.body: A US partnership between refrigerated storage company US Cold Storage and food waste recovery company Divert has turned unsold food and beverage products into renewable energy, fertiliser and recovered water. The programme covered seven facilities in California in its first 15 months and processed more than 2.5 million pounds of products that could no longer be sold.Instead of sending these goods to landfill, the companies found a way to recover useful resources from them. According to Divert’s press release, the products were transported to its Integrated Diversion & Energy Facility in Turlock, California. At the facility, specialised machines separated the food from its packaging before anaerobic digestion technology processed the material to produce renewable energy, fertiliser and recovered water.How Divert and US Cold Storage partnered to process unsold foodThe partnership brought together Divert, a circular economy company, and United States Cold Storage, a provider of refrigerated warehousing and logistics. Unsold products from seven US Cold facilities in California were sent to Divert's Turlock facility.The arrangement covered products that could no longer be sold. Its platform was designed to respond to customer needs and recover value from unsold goods rather than treating them only as waste.The company said the programme helped US Cold expand its sustainable product destruction work across several locations. This was supported by dynamic pricing and routing materials to suitable facilities. The partnership was presented as a way to support brands' sustainability commitments through the end of the supply chain.How the food waste recovery system produces renewable energy and fertiliserOnce opportunities to sell or donate products had been exhausted, US Cold sent the material to Divert's Integrated Diversion & Energy Facility in Turlock, California. There, the company used proprietary High-Recovery Depackaging technology and anaerobic digestion to process it. The treatment produced renewable natural gas, nutrient-rich agricultural fertilisers and recovered water.It supplied fertiliser and soil amendments to regional partners, including Western Milling and Crème Brulee Farming Co. These products supported local farms growing new food. The process was intended to keep value circulating locally while providing US Cold and its customers with secure handling, documentation, and environmental benefits.The partnership processed 2.5 million pounds of unsold products in 15 monthsThe partnership processed more than 2.5 million pounds of unsold food and beverage products in its first 15 months. Divert reported that the material generated more than 8,500 MMBtu of renewable natural gas. The work also avoided about 450 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions.The company said this was equal to about 40 trips around the equator for an average gasoline-powered vehicle. Oatly products moving through US Cold's network were also included.The partnership processed 126,000 pounds of Oatly products, generating nearly 80 MMBtu of renewable natural gas and avoiding about 4 metric tons of CO2 equivalent emissions.Divert plans to turn food waste into enough energy for thousands of homesReportedly, its Turlock facility could produce several resources when operating at full capacity. It could generate enough renewable energy each year to power more than 4,000 homes. Its output could also include enough liquid nitrogen fertiliser to support 112 million pounds of strawberries and enough soil amendment to treat up to 2,000 acres of farmland.The company estimated that the facility could offset 23,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions annually. More than 7,800 customer locations across the food supply chain were already using its Circularity Platform.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: British Airways passenger Ed Butler spent more than £2,000 on a family hotel after a cancelled flight, then took the airline to court over £12 in unpaid interest and won
articles.summary: A British Airways cancelled flight, a hotel bill of more than £2,000 and an unpaid interest claim of just £12 ended in a County Court victory for
articles.body: A British Airways cancelled flight, a hotel bill of more than £2,000 and an unpaid interest claim of just £12 ended in a County Court victory for passenger Ed Butler. Butler, 43, a businessman, was flying home from a holiday in the United States with his wife and four children in July 2025 when a technical fault delayed their journey by a day. The airline told the family to pay for accommodation and meals up front and reclaim the money afterwards, which began a months-long dispute that eventually reached a judge. A County Court ruling does not set binding legal precedent.How British Airways offered only part of the hotel bill, then paid in full after a legal threat from Ed ButlerAccording to National Solicitors, the airline initially offered just £800 towards the hotel and meals, leaving the family more than £1,500 out of pocket. The matter dragged on until Butler threatened legal action in September 2025, prompting the airline to settle the full amount, which reached him in October 2025.Butler argued that the money owed to him was effectively a debt, so he was entitled to statutory interest. He charged 8 per cent for the 35 days between issuing his legal claim and receiving the reimbursement. The airline denied owing it, arguing that the law did not require interest on compensation. Butler told The Telegraph that, after being dragged through unnecessary complaints and court proceedings, he was not prepared to back down. He added that he believes the airline has a policy of obstructing claims in the hope that people give up or claim through their insurance instead of being paid what is legally due.The court awarded £11.76 in interest, a £181 court fee and nothing for the broken shower Uxbridge County Court ruled in Butler’s favour in May 2026. It did not uphold a separate £100 claim he made over a broken shower at the airline’s lounge in Boston, during a different trip to the United States in summer 2025. Butler said the broken shower meant he could not freshen up before the overnight flight back to Britain.National Solicitors reported that the judgment could encourage other passengers to seek interest on delayed reimbursement claims. Consumer expert Martyn James told The Telegraph that although small claims is the lowest court, the ruling is still a legal judgment that others could argue is a precedent, and a judge may interpret it that way. He added that, despite clear passenger rights when flights are cancelled, some airlines remain reluctant to follow the law, often doing only what it strictly requires and sometimes only after legal action is threatened. A British Airways spokesperson said that on the rare occasions cancellations occur, the airline does its best to make things right, and that where claims meet the legislative requirements, its teams work to process them as quickly as possible.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘50cr Indians defeated poverty’: PM Modi counters Rahul’s ‘economic disaster’ remark, cites World Bank figures
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday highlighted India's economic growth and poverty reduction at the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and
articles.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday highlighted India's economic growth and poverty reduction at the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) annual general meeting and convention, a day after Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi described the country as being in the grip of an “economic disaster”.Speaking at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, the PM said India was the world's fastest-growing major economy, with growth projected at around 7 per cent.‘India is the world's fastest-growing major economy’“Today, India is the world's fastest-growing major economy, projected to grow at around 7%. In October, India's goods exports reached nearly $50 billion, our highest-ever monthly goods export,” Modi said.He added that agencies including Moody's Ratings, S&P Global Ratings, Fitch Ratings, the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank were revising their growth forecasts for India upwards.‘50 crore Indians have defeated poverty’Citing a World Bank report, Modi said 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty in the past 12 to 13 years. He contrasted this with the Congress-era 'Garibi Hatao' slogan.“In the 1970s, when the 'Garibi Hatao' slogan was given, India's population was around 50 crore; poverty could have been eradicated then too, but FICCI is a witness that there was a flaw in policies and, unfortunately, a lack of the right intention,” he said.“When we worked with the right policies and the right intention, 50 crore poor people came out of poverty in just 12–13 years,” he added. PM's remarks came after Rahul Gandhi, speaking at Columbia University in New York, said India was “sitting on an economic disaster”, citing unemployment, a struggling manufacturing sector and problems in education.‘My countrymen deserve top quality’The Prime Minister also challenged businesses to stop treating Indian consumers as a market for lower-quality products.“Do not take 140 crore Indians for granted as an assured market where anything will sell. Even today, sellers tell customers 'this is export quality' to convince them it is good. What do you take our countrymen for? Do they not deserve good quality? This mindset must change; my countrymen deserve top quality,” he said.‘Doors have opened for you’: Modi to industryReferring to India's free trade agreements with major economies, Modi urged businesses to take advantage of expanded market access.“India has signed Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with several major economies; doors have opened for you. Have you planned to seize this opportunity? If you do not take advantage of all my hard work, who will?” he said.‘Did you increase salaries or hire more staff?’Modi also cited tax reforms, including the reduction in the basic corporate tax rate from 30 per cent to 22 per cent and the exemption from income tax on earnings up to Rs 12 lakh.“Did you increase your employees' salaries or hire more staff?” he asked business leaders, while highlighting simplified tax returns and faster refunds.Recalling India's journey from the “License Quota Raj” to the “Fragile Five” period, Modi said young people, farmers, workers and industry leaders had helped transform the economy over the past 12 years.FICCI's centenary year marks 100 years since its establishment on April 7, 1927. The convention comes amid a wider political debate over economic growth, jobs and the distribution of its benefits.‘Pharmacy of the world’ still imports APIs, bulk drugsModi also called on the pharmaceutical industry to reduce dependence on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), bulk drugs and drug intermediates.“India is called the ‘pharmacy of the world,’ yet it imports billions of dollars' worth of APIs, bulk drugs, and drug intermediates every year,” he said.“There are hundreds of categories in which we currently depend on imports. Our pharmaceutical industry must understand which ingredients we can manufacture in India. In which areas can we invest in new technology and large production plants to become competitive with other countries?” he added.PM urges industry to invest in agricultureThe Prime Minister also called for greater private investment in agriculture and urged businesses to develop products for overseas markets.“I would urge you to increase your industry’s investment in India’s agricultural sector. Set up reliable procurement systems with specific overseas markets in mind, and develop products for which there is demand there, so that Indian products can become our calling card around the world,” Modi said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Since 2018, Colombia’s Isla Fuerte has placed 25 clay figures underwater to shelter corals threatened by tourism and climate change; coral was seen growing on them by 2024
articles.summary: Discover how Isla Fuerte in Colombia is using art to protect coral reefs from the impacts of tourism and climate change, showcasing a unique underwater gallery that promotes coral growth.
articles.body: What if the answer to a damaged reef was a piece of art? Off Colombia’s Caribbean coast, one island is putting that idea to the test. Since 2018, Isla Fuerte has placed 25 clay figures underwater to shelter corals threatened by tourism and climate change. A 2024 AFP report, published on Phys.org, described it as Colombia’s first underwater art gallery.A fashion designer with a big ideaThe project, known as MUSZIF, was started by Tatiana Orrego, a fashion designer living on the island. She explained to AFP that she had observed a decline in the island’s natural reefs and saw an opportunity to protect corals through art. Two potters, Hugo Osorio and Pedro Fuentes, work together to sculpt the figures on her commission. The figures are about 1.5 metres in height and placed on the seabed at a depth of about six metres. Their design is inspired by the ancient sculptures made by the Zenú people, who lived in the Caribbean part of Colombia before the arrival of the Spanish. The 2024 report said that another 25 would follow, but a 2025 Columbia One report still lists 25 statues.Why corals need a hand Colombia’s corals cover an area the size of 100,000 football fields, but more than two-thirds had already suffered bleaching, according to the environment ministry. Bleaching occurs when stressed corals expel tiny algae living inside them and can lead to coral die-off. This can end up impacting ecosystems, tourism and food security. The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) confirmed the fourth global bleaching event in April 2024. In 2026, it reported that the event likely ended in mid-2025, after bleaching-level heat stress reached 84% of the world’s reef area. NOAA says such events are linked to warming oceans but that bleached corals can recover if the stress disappears.A place for visitors to go instead Tourism adds another layer of pressure. The same report noted that some tourists are known to pluck chunks of coral to bring to the surface while others harm the reefs by walking over them. As Orrego puts it, “People don't understand that coral is a living being.” The gallery presents another way out. It attracts about 2,000 visitors a year, apart from fish and divers, and Orrego calls it an alternative space for tourists that doesn’t strain the natural reefs. She seeded the clay figures with baby corals, saying they offered an ideal surface for growth; by 2024, she had seen the corals take off.What research says about artificial reefsIsla Fuerte is not the first place to try out this idea. Higgins, Metaxas and Scheibling’s 2022 PLOS ONE review, ‘A systematic review of artificial reefs as platforms for coral reef research and conservation,’ found that artificial reefs have been used on coral reefs since the 1980s. The authors concluded that they are more likely to help by providing nursery habitat or a surface on which corals can settle. The review noted that the structures are usually too small to cope with regional coral losses. Studies are also often too short, less than five years, to determine long-term trends in coral cover.A small step, not a cure These limits matter to Isla Fuerte. AFP’s report only retells Orrego’s story of the coral growth and doesn’t refer to any survey data. So it is unclear how many corals have settled or how they will fare in future heat waves. The review also suggests that the projects that promote local cultural values have potential to raise awareness of reef decline, if prioritised and properly monitored. Still, the project gives corals a surface to grow on, gives tourists another place to visit and, in Osorio’s words, helps preserve Zenú culture. It might not be a perfect fix, but it shows how art, culture and conservation can walk together to save the struggling corals.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Discover how Spain's innovative artificial reef off Cádiz has dramatically reduced illegal trawling and boosted local artisanal fishing catches, safeguarding marine resources.
articles.body: Spain, between 2000 and 2005, had developed an underwater barrier system off the coast of Cádiz to tackle illegal bottom trawling that had threatened both marine resources and small-scale fishing communities. Instead of relying solely on enforcement patrols, the project used hundreds of reinforced-concrete structures and placed them along the routes that were favoured by trawlers. The Sancti Petri artificial reef was built with the aim of making it difficult for prohibited fishing gear to operate in the protected area. In its 2010 Quality Status Report, the OSPAR Commission noted a significant decline in illegal trawling activity and an increase in artisanal catches after the reef’s construction.An underwater barrier made to tackle illegal fishing The Sancti Petri reef lies in the Gulf of Cádiz, which is off southwestern Spain. The reef is at depths of approximately 15 to 40 metres. The area supported substantial artisanal fishing activity; however, illegal bottom-trawling vessels continued operating in waters where this kind of fishing method was prohibited. Fishing pressure increased because of this activity, and fishing nets and other equipment used by the small-scale fishing boats were at risk of being damaged by this. In 2000, the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food began developing the reef, with the stated objectives of protecting fish populations, reducing pressure from illegal catches, preventing damage to artisanal fishing gear and limiting conflicts between the groups involved in fishing. The structure was completed in 2005.It is worth noting that the project did not create one singular continuous underwater wall. Instead, the engineers designed it into three reef zones, each containing three barrier systems positioned perpendicular to the routes that the trawlers favoured. One nautical mile of open water separated the barriers. Each barrier was rectangular in layout and measured between two and four kilometres in length and approximately 200 metres in width. The individual modules, on the other hand, were spaced approximately 75 to 200 metres apart, thus creating obstacles intended to interfere with the passage of bottom-trawling equipment.Every module was a reinforced-concrete cylinder that weighed approximately 5.5 tonnes and was supported by a three-metre base which was designed to prevent it from sinking. A total of 569 modules were deployed, as noted by the OSPAR Commission report. Spain’s Ministry of Agriculture lists 569 modules for the Sancti Petri installation and records 2000 as its installation year. This year marks the beginning of the installation period, as development continued until the complex was completed in 2005.Monitoring results beneath the surfaceAuthorities assessed the reef’s condition through recurring structural and functional surveys. According to OSPAR, these inspections were conducted every two years using side-scan sonar. This helped them to examine the arrangement and condition of the underwater structures. Furthermore, fishing activity and artisanal catches were monitored separately, and fishermen were consulted through opinion polls.The organisation described a dramatic decrease in illegal trawling activity in its report. It also observed an increase in artisanal catches. However, these two findings should be distinguished, as the report does not provide a quantified percentage reduction in illegal trawling or a precise figure for the increase in catches. The findings therefore support the conclusion that the reef helped protect local fishing activity. Though, they should not be treated as proof of a measured recovery in fish populations.The project also had some drawbacks. The 2010 report noted occasional entanglement of trammel nets in the structures, although this did not appear to create much of a ghost-fishing problem, in which lost or abandoned fishing gear continues catching marine animals. The assessment found that no major environmental impact had been detected, attributing this partly to the artificial reef’s limited physical footprint and the stability of the materials it was constructed with. This was a finding from the monitoring available at the time, rather than a claim that artificial reefs carry no environmental risks.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Elon Musk says he feels ‘pretty foolish’ after spending hundreds of millions backing Republicans in US midterms
articles.summary: Elon Musk expresses regret over his substantial financial support for Republican candidates in the 2026 US midterm elections amidst major party losses, while advocating for moderate political views and distancing from the MAGA movement.
articles.body: Elon Musk has said he feels “pretty foolish” about spending hundreds of millions of dollars backing Republican candidates in the 2026 US midterm elections, after the party suffered major losses in both chambers of Congress.During The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the billionaire also distanced himself from the MAGA movement, describing his political views as “quite moderate” and saying he does not hold “extreme political views”.Musk, who served in President Donald Trump’s administration in 2025, spent heavily through political action committees supporting Republican candidates in House and Senate races. His spending reportedly reached nearly $475 million during this election cycle, according to NYT.Texas was among his biggest political investments. More than $150 million of his fortune went towards a group supporting Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, according to CBS News. However, Paxton lost to Democrat James Talarico, who made Musk’s backing of his opponent part of his campaign message.Democrats also won the Texas governor’s race, with Gina Hinojosa defeating Republican Greg Abbott. The result marked a significant political shift in a state where Musk has established major operations for Tesla and SpaceX.The billionaire told interviewer Andrew Ross Sorkin that his main objective had been to help Republicans retain their Senate majority and ensure neither party gained control of the presidency and both chambers of Congress in 2029. He said the effort had failed.“Obviously, the Republicans were routed in this election, and … I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it. Or maybe it would have been much worse without that,” Musk said.He added that, given the outcome, he would have approached the spending differently. “Probably if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money,” he said.Musk said his intention was to maintain political “checks and balances”, rather than secure an overwhelming majority for either party. He also argued that campaign spending could not determine election outcomes on its own.When Sorkin raised questions about Musk’s past comments on immigration and his association with the MAGA movement, the billionaire rejected the label.“I’m not MAGA. ... I’m not sure what MAGA means, but I don’t think I’m, like, if it means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that,” he said.“I think there are positives and negatives in both parties,” Musk added.The remarks mark a shift from his public support for Trump during the 2024 presidential campaign. At a rally that year, Musk told supporters: “I’m not just MAGA, I’m dark MAGA.”Musk and Trump had a public falling-out last year but have since appeared to restore their relationship. The billionaire travelled to China this week as part of the US president's visit to the country.His political involvement is now expected to face scrutiny from Democrats, who have said they intend to investigate the Trump administration after taking control of Congress. Musk is expected to be among the subjects of potential oversight inquiries, including questions about his role in the administration and his business interests.Despite the Democrats' victory in Texas, Musk said he did not expect the change in leadership to create difficulties for his companies. He described Hinojosa as “quite moderate” and said he believed business operations in the state would remain unaffected.Musk also pushed back against suggestions from some Democratic lawmakers that he should face legal scrutiny over his political and government activities, describing such comments as “a little over the top”.“There are definitely a few people grumpy about ... my funding in this past election,” he told Sorkin.You use AI every day. articles.title: A New Jersey boy was allegedly falsely blamed for a viral TikTok school shooting list, kept out of classes for over a year and bullied for years afterward; his parents have now sued school officials
articles.summary: A New Jersey family has filed a lawsuit against a school district, accusing administrators of failing to protect their son after classmates allegedly
articles.body: A New Jersey family has filed a lawsuit against a school district, accusing administrators of failing to protect their son after classmates allegedly falsely linked him to a viral TikTok school shooting threat. The student was kept away from school for more than a year and continued to face harassment after returning, according to a report by Daily Voice. The Ridgewood Blog also reported on the allegations, detailing the family’s claims that school officials treated the boy as a potential threat rather than addressing the bullying directed at him. The lawsuit was filed on November 5 in Bergen County Superior Court. It names the Ramsey Board of Education, Ramsey Borough School District, more than a dozen school officials, seven students and a parent as defendants. The student, identified in the complaint only as T.A., attended Eric S. Smith Middle School before moving on to Ramsey High School.According to the complaint, the situation began in January 2022, when a group of students allegedly spread rumours about T.A.‘s sexual orientation. Matters escalated when several students created an anonymous TikTok account featuring a list of students allegedly marked for killing on January 31, 2022. The account’s creators reportedly identified T.A. as the person behind the post, an accusation his family maintains was false. When T.A.‘s mother approached school administrators to report the allegations against her son, officials allegedly contacted the police instead. Officers subsequently arrived at the family’s home and took the boy to the Ramsey police station for questioning. He was released the same day, but the school reportedly informed his parents that he could not return to classes. The complaint states that T.A. remained on home instruction until March 2023, spending more than a year away from regular school attendance. The district allegedly classified the period as an out-of-school suspension.The allegations continued after his return to schoolReturning to the classroom did little to end the problems, according to the lawsuit. Students allegedly continued to associate T.A. with the TikTok threat, repeatedly questioning whether he owned weapons and suggesting that he intended to carry out an attack at school. One incident described in the complaint took place in October 2023 during a band class. A teacher allegedly expressed feeling threatened when T.A. was putting away a pair of scissors, while another student suggested that the boy might use them to stab someone.The accusations also reportedly affected the family’s life outside school. During the same month, a student and her mother allegedly told the family’s pastor that T.A. had been expelled and was stalking the student. The pastor subsequently asked the family to leave the church. According to the complaint, he later apologised and invited them back after learning about the accusations against the boy.The family further alleges that school administrators failed to respond appropriately to repeated complaints about harassment. In September 2024, Ramsey High School Principal Michael Thumm allegedly told T.A. and his parents to stop submitting harassment, intimidation and bullying complaints.The situation reportedly continued into 2026, with the complaint describing several additional accusations and physical incidents. In January, a student allegedly accused T.A. of rape, while another student claimed the following month that he was attempting to poison classmates using fentanyl-laced candy. Physical confrontations followed. In March 2026, a student allegedly punched T.A. in the stomach during an auto shop class while a teacher watched. The teacher reportedly responded by telling the student to watch his language. In June, another student allegedly slapped T.A. across the face, breaking his glasses.Family seeks damages over alleged school failuresThe lawsuit argues that school officials repeatedly failed to investigate complaints, address the alleged harassment or provide adequate protection. The family also maintains that T.A., who receives special education services, experienced significant physical and emotional harm as a result of the incidents. According to the complaint, the family has spent more than $3,600 on medical expenses related to the alleged injuries.The legal action includes claims of negligence, discrimination under New Jersey’s Law Against Discrimination, defamation, and intentional and negligent infliction of emotional distress, among other allegations. The family is seeking compensatory and punitive damages, reimbursement of attorney’s fees and a jury trial. However, the complaint does not specify the amount of compensation being sought.The case was filed by attorney Frederick E. Gerson of Feitlin, Youngman, Karas & Gerson LLC, based in Glen Rock, New Jersey. Ramsey Public Schools Superintendent Dr. Andrew C. Matteo said the district does not comment on pending litigation when approached by Daily Voice.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Ukraine's third strike in four days disrupts rail traffic on Kerch Bridge
articles.summary: A Ukrainian attack on the Kerch Bridge, which connects Russia with Crimea, stopped train services on Thursday.
articles.body: A Ukrainian attack on the Kerch Bridge, which connects Russia with Crimea, stopped train services on Thursday. It was the third Ukrainian attack on the key bridge in four days, a Russian official said. Earlier strikes had also forced authorities to suspend road traffic.According to news agency AP, the latest attack took place overnight. Train services were halted while officials checked the damage. However, traffic was expected to resume around 4 pm local time on Thursday, Sergei Aksyonov, the Moscow-appointed head of Crimea, said.The attacks came as Russian president Vladimir Putin met Chinese President Xi Jinping and US president Donald Trump in China. They appeared to challenge Moscow's claim that Russia's victory in the war was inevitable. They also showed that Ukraine continues to have the ability to strike important Russian targets.The Kerch Bridge is a major route for transporting military equipment and civilian supplies to Crimea. Russia seized the peninsula in 2014, a move widely condemned internationally. The bridge has become a symbol of Moscow's control over the region and a key target for Ukrainian forces.The latest attack came hours before talks between Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, and European leaders in Berlin on Thursday.Kushner and Witkoff have been leading US efforts to end the war, which began with Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They have recently helped organise fresh discussions, but the talks have yet to produce a major breakthrough.In a post on X on Thursday, Kushner said Washington wanted to strengthen coordination with Ukraine and European countries. He said the meeting would focus on building a common position on the key elements of a lasting peace deal.The discussions will also cover the role of Ukraine's European supporters in future security arrangements.Ukraine wants firm guarantees to prevent another Russian invasion. Moscow, meanwhile, wants to keep NATO away from its borders.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Bloodshed in Karachi, Hyderabad': Why Bilawal Bhutto is opposing plan to redraw Pakistan's map
articles.summary: Pakistan Peoples Party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has strongly opposed the proposal to divide Pakistan into multiple provinces, warning against any
articles.body: Pakistan Peoples Party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has strongly opposed the proposal to divide Pakistan into multiple provinces, warning against any attempt to split Sindh by force.He cautioned that such a move could trigger violence and bloodshed in Karachi and Hyderabad, Pakistan-based Geo TV reported.The proposal to redraw Pakistan's political map has reportedly found support among several leaders in the country's power corridors, including army chief Asim Munir and defence minister Khawaja Asif.Speaking at an event at the Karachi Press Club, Bilawal said any forced division of the province would create social divisions and push ordinary people towards violence, Geo TV reported.“If the province is divided by force, society will be divided, it will lead to enmity, ordinary people will take up arms, and the bloodshed will not be limited to a single death,” he said.The remarks come amid discussions in Pakistan about reorganising its administrative structure by dividing its four provinces into smaller units. Reports have suggested that army chief Asim Munir is considering a plan to create 12 to 15 provinces or reorganise the country into as many as 160 smaller administrative units to address governance challenges.The proposal has gained support from some senior ministers, but faces opposition from political parties, particularly over the possible division of Sindh, where the Bhutto-Zardari family and the PPP have a strong political base.Bilawal said the PPP was not opposed to creating new provinces but insisted that any such move must follow the wishes of the people and the constitutional process.“The PPP supports the creation of provinces in line with the wishes of the people, the Constitution and the law. Where we are opposing, it is over force and coercion. We do not want division through force,” he said.He also questioned suggestions that a referendum could be used to decide the issue, saying the Constitution already provided a procedure for creating new provinces.“If you are looking for an unconstitutional method, how can the PPP be with you?” he asked.Bilawal further said referendums in Pakistan's history had been used for undemocratic purposes. “It is not about a referendum, it is about intent,” he said.Why is Pakistan considering more provincesThe proposal to increase the number of provinces from four to as many as 12 has gained momentum, with supporters arguing that smaller administrative units could improve governance and public services.Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif has backed the idea, saying the country's growing population requires smaller provinces for more efficient administration.Speaking to Geo News, Asif said Pakistan could consider creating 12 provinces, provided their boundaries were based on administrative needs rather than linguistic, ethnic or political considerations.However, the proposal faces a major political challenge, with no consensus among leading parties, particularly over the possible division of Sindh.You use AI every day. articles.title: ​A Broome woman's GP told her to bite off a lump on her tongue; she was later referred to a specialist by her dentist, who diagnosed tongue cancer, and surgery removed more than a third of her tongue
articles.summary: Monica Frain, a Broome resident, noticed a small lump on her tongue in late 2022.
articles.body: Monica Frain, a Broome resident, noticed a small lump on her tongue in late 2022. Her GP reportedly told her to bite it off, but a routine dental check-up changed the course of events. Her dentist flagged the growth and referred her to a specialist, who diagnosed tongue cancer, ABC News reported. Frain underwent five hours of surgery to remove more than a third of her tongue.Her GP told her to bite it offMonica Frain first noticed a pinhead-sized lump on her tongue in late 2022. For months, the lump bothered her. In fact, she grew more annoyed than alarmed. She had recently undergone cardiac surgery and assumed that the lump could have been caused by the breathing tube placed during the procedure. She consulted a local general practitioner, who assured her there was nothing to worry about. In fact, the GP told her to bite the lump off.A routine dental examination flagged the growthAfter the GP's consultation, Monica Frain went for a routine dental check-up. Dentist Stephanie Mulcahy saw the lump and did not wait to see whether it would go away. She immediately referred Frain to an oral medicine specialist. "While it didn't look sinister, I wanted confirmation of what it was," Dr Mulcahy told the broadcaster.The cancer diagnosisGetting a specialist opinion is difficult in Broome and across the Kimberley, the far north of Western Australia. Most specialists fly in from Perth, which is about 2,240 kilometres south, and work to a strict rotating schedule. Since Dr Mulcahy told her it wasn't ideal to wait, Frain flew to Perth in early 2023. She consulted an oral medicine specialist, who ordered a biopsy. The result showed squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). It is the most common form of tongue cancer, according to Cancer Research UK. Squamous cells are flat, skin-like cells that cover the lining of the mouth, nose, larynx, thyroid and throat. Since the cancer was detected early, it had not spread, and surgery was sufficient to treat it. However, the procedure still meant removing more than a third of her tongue. The surgery lasted five hours.Why abnormal lumps should not be dismissedFrain says she is ‘extremely grateful’ to Dr Mulcahy for her medical advice. "If Dr Steph had not pushed for me to go and see a specialist and have it removed, I could have been in a terrible state," she told the broadcaster.For Dr Mulcahy, though, it was simply part of her responsibility as a dentist to investigate anything that appeared unusual and ensure her patient received the right care. She has seen how these cancers can progress. She has identified tongue cancer in other patients, and one of them died of the disease.Oral and maxillofacial pathology specialist Omar Kujan told the broadcaster that Frain's case shows how much timing matters. "Regular dental check-ups can save lives by identifying early warning signs that people may not notice themselves," Dr Kujan said.The specialist also added that oral cancer can develop without pain or obvious symptoms. "Early diagnosis significantly improves the chances of successful treatment and survival. Timely access to oral healthcare must be a priority, particularly in regional and remote Australia."Tongue cancer is a type of head and neck cancer. Symptoms include a spot or lump on the tongue that does not go away. Smoking, alcohol consumption and infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) are some of the risk factors.You use AI every day.
